discovery: Discovery of the two-dimensional electron system at oxide interfaces (LaAlO3/SrTiO3) and its emergent electronic phases

nominees.name: Harold Y. Hwang
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Jochen Mannhart
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: correlated oxide heterostructures and interfaces
motivation: In 2004 Ohtomo and Hwang showed that joining two band insulators, LaAlO3 and SrTiO3, with atomic-layer precision produces a high-mobility two-dimensional electron system at their interface. This established that interfaces between complex oxides can host electronic states that neither constituent possesses. Mannhart and co-workers then demonstrated a critical thickness for conduction, electric-field switching of the interface, and interface superconductivity. With others, these results revealed tunable superconductivity, magnetism and strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling in one engineered layer. Together the work created a new field, 'oxide interface physics': designing quantum phases atom by atom rather than finding them in bulk crystals. It has changed how physicists think about polar discontinuities, orbital reconstruction and electrostatic control of correlated electrons. It also laid the foundations for oxide electronics and for the later discovery of nickelate superconductivity. It is a paradigm shift of lasting influence.
